security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's CSR dispatch table does not register tinfo (0x7A4) and tcontrol (0x7A5) as valid Debug/Trace CSRs, causing accesses to these newly-allocated CSR addresses to fall through to the default unimplemented-CSR trap path (illegal instruction), or worse, to alias onto an unrelated CSR or return stale/uninitialized data from an unvalidated read path.
security_spec.summary: Newly-allocated Sdtrig CSRs tinfo (0x7A4) and tcontrol (0x7A5) must be registered in QEMU's CSR lookup table; absence causes illegal-instruction traps on valid guest CSR accesses, breaking debug/trace trigger functionality expected by spec-compliant guest software.

findings.finding: CSR tcontrol (0x7A5) is missing from the CSR dispatch table. The RISC-V ISA manual (csrs.adoc lines 1001-1030) allocates 0x7A5 as the 'Trigger control register' (tcontrol) in the Debug/Trace Registers block alongside tselect, tdata1-3, tinfo, and mcontext. No CSR_TCONTROL macro is defined in cpu_bits.h, no read/write handler is implemented in csr.c or debug.c, and no entry exists in the csr_ops table. Any machine-mode access to CSR 0x7A5 hits the NULL predicate check in riscv_csrrw_check() (line 5588) and returns RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST — the emulated guest sees an illegal instruction exception where a valid CSR read/write should succeed. This causes function_loss: debugging tools and external debuggers that rely on tcontrol for trigger configuration will malfunction.
findings.snippet:
/* Debug CSRs */
    [CSR_TSELECT]   =  { "tselect",  debug, read_tselect,  write_tselect  },
    [CSR_TDATA1]    =  { "tdata1",   debug, read_tdata,    write_tdata    },
    [CSR_TDATA2]    =  { "tdata2",   debug, read_tdata,    write_tdata    },
    [CSR_TDATA3]    =  { "tdata3",   debug, read_tdata,    write_tdata    },
    [CSR_TINFO]     =  { "tinfo",    debug, read_tinfo,    write_ignore   },
    /* CSR_TCONTROL (0x7A5) is MISSING — gap before MCONTEXT */
    [CSR_MCONTEXT]  =  { "mcontext", debug, read_mcontext, write_mcontext },

spec_citations.excerpt: Debug/Trace Registers (shared with Debug Mode): 0x7A0 tselect, 0x7A1 tdata1, 0x7A2 tdata2, 0x7A3 tdata3, 0x7A4 tinfo, 0x7A5 tcontrol, 0x7A8 mcontext. tcontrol is described as 'Trigger control register.'

findings.finding: CSR tinfo (0x7A4) is correctly implemented and registered. CSR_TINFO is defined in cpu_bits.h:463, read_tinfo() delegates to tinfo_csr_read() in debug.c:918, and the CSR is registered as read-only (write_ignore) in the dispatch table at line 6378. This matches the spec allocation at csrs.adoc lines 1001-1030.

CSR_TCONTROL (0x7A5) macro is missing from cpu_bits.h. The Debug/Trace register block defines CSR_TSELECT (0x7A0) through CSR_TINFO (0x7A4), then jumps directly to CSR_MCONTEXT (0x7A8), skipping 0x7A5 (tcontrol) entirely. Without this macro, the CSR dispatch table in csr.c cannot register tcontrol.
findings.snippet:
/* Debug/Trace Registers (shared with Debug Mode) */
#define CSR_TSELECT         0x7a0
#define CSR_TDATA1          0x7a1
#define CSR_TDATA2          0x7a2
#define CSR_TDATA3          0x7a3
#define CSR_TINFO           0x7a4
/* CSR_TCONTROL (0x7A5) is MISSING */
#define CSR_MCONTEXT        0x7a8

spec_citations.excerpt: Debug/Trace Registers (shared with Debug Mode): 0x7A5 tcontrol — Trigger control register.

findings.finding: No tcontrol read/write handler exists in debug.c. The file implements tselect, tdata1-3, and tinfo handling via tinfo_csr_read(), but tcontrol has no CSR read/write functions. Any attempt to access tcontrol will fail at the CSR dispatch layer before reaching debug.c.
findings.snippet: (no tcontrol handler — the string 'tcontrol' does not appear anywhere in target/riscv/)
